intended_object: The pure tensor m ⊗_A n in the balanced tensor product M ⊗_A N, where M is a right A-module and N is a left A-module, both k-modules. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: `tmul m n` is `mk k A m n`, and `mk` is `(TensorProduct.mk k M N).compr₂ (mkQ k A)`. So it is the image of m ⊗ₜ[k] n in the quotient of M ⊗[k] N by the k-span of the relations (m·a) ⊗ n − m ⊗ (a·n), which is exactly the standard pure tensor in M ⊗_A N. The lemmas that follow show the expected bilinearity (`add_tmul`, `tmul_add`, `smul_tmul`) and the zero lemmas (`zero_tmul`, `tmul_zero`). The generality matches the enclosing construction: k is a commutative ring, A is any semiring, M is a right A-module via Aᵐᵒᵖ and N is a left A-module. Additive groups are needed only because the carrier is a submodule quotient, so this is not a restriction coming from `tmul`. Mathlib has no balanced tensor product over a noncommutative ring; its `TensorProduct.tmul` only covers a commutative base ring, so nothing in Mathlib is more general.
